title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 81
paragraphs: After this the Thebans, having made an attempt with the alliance of the sons of Aeacus and having been roughly handled by the Athenians, sent again and gave them back the sons of Aeacus and asked them for men. So the Aeginetans, exalted by great prosperity and recalling an ancient grudge against the Athenians, at the Thebans' request began a war against the Athenians without notice. For while the Athenians were intent on the Boeotians, the Aeginetans sailed against them to Attica with warships and devastated Phalerum and many other demes in the rest of the coastal region; and by so doing they deeply stirred the Athenians' resentment.
